label: diffuse token-identity unit (weak preference for h/x/e/n inputs during the original phase)
explanation: Diffuse, broadly tuned candidate coordinate (5% of steps, ~40% of sequences). The strongest single signal is the input token: h (35% active rate, 7x lift), then x, e, n (2-3x), plus a long tail of other tokens. Activation is boosted when the previous inputs are also from {h,x,e,n,o,v} (precision rises to 0.73 but recall drops to 0.17). About 64% of activation mass is in the original phase, mostly at t=1-3; it is weak at t=0 and nearly silent at the delimiter. Copy-phase activity (35% of mass) peaks at recall_idx 1 and when outputting p/q/2, and does not follow the h/x/e/n input preference (h as a copy-phase input rarely fires). The largest activations occur on h at the first copy step after a sequence that starts with h. No compact predicate does better than F1 ~0.4 on dev (best 0.40; the chosen predicate gets 0.37 F1 with 0.50 mass recall), so the unit is not explained.
